title: Mountain Meadows and Wild Forest
lead: The wildest national park in Poland. Mountain meadows, bison, wolves, and villages that disappeared from the map after 1947.
body:
The Wildest Park in Poland

Bieszczady National Park is the wildest and most inaccessible national park in Poland. It covers the highest parts of the Bieszczady — Połonina Wetlińska and Caryńska, Tarnica, Halicz, Wielka Rawka. This is a land of endless horizons where nature rules by its own laws.

The park is home to the largest predators in Poland — bison, wolves, lynxes, and bears live here. These animals are rarely seen, but their presence is felt in every corner of the park. While walking through the mountain meadows, it is worth remembering that you are not alone here — this is the territory of wild nature.

Villages That Disappeared

Bieszczady National Park is also a land of memory. After 1947, as part of Operation Vistula, almost all inhabitants of these lands — Boykos and Lemkos — were displaced. Many villages disappeared from the map, and today only cottage foundations, old orchards, and lonely churches can be found.

Traces of former inhabitants are everywhere — in the landscape, in place names, in old cemeteries. It is worth walking through the park slowly, stopping at each trace and remembering that this land has its own history that must be respected.
tip: Bring provisions and water for the whole day — there are not many shops or restaurants in the Bieszczady. The mountain meadows are beautiful but demanding.
